turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I fear no man, Sandip, but I am not blind to the dangers that threaten us. Your actions are stirring unrest, and I will not stand by while my people suffer.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your tenants are not puppets to be controlled with threats, Nikhil. They are the very lifeblood of our society, and they see the difference between your weakness and my passion. Do not mistake my zeal for oppression.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your zeal may be clear to some, Sandip, but it is not lost on me that your methods are divisive and dangerous. I will not tolerate further interference with my people's well-being.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Divisive and dangerous, you say? I see a society yearning for change, Nikhil. Your tenants are not puppets, but they are waking up to the reality you choose to ignore. And as for the Mussulmans, let them come. I stand ready to face them, unlike some who hide behind their tenants.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I do not hide behind my tenants, Sandip. I stand for their protection and the stability of our society. Your provocations will not be tolerated.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I... I am worried about the tension between you both. And the people... they are not just puppets or lifeblood, they are human beings with their own struggles and fears.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, my dear, worry not. The fire of change is not quenched by mere threats. And to you, Nikhil, let the truth be known: I do not shy away from conflict, for it is through conflict that we find the path to true progress.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I see that you both have strong convictions, but can't we find a way to move forward without causing harm to others?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Progress through conflict? Your methods are reckless, Sandip. I will not allow my people to become collateral in your ambitions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your heart is in the right place, but your vision is too narrow. The storm clouds of change gather, and it is through these tempests that we see the light of a new dawn.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The light of a new dawn? Your rhetoric sounds noble, but it hides your true intent to exploit and divide. Cease your manipulative schemes or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Exploitation and division, you say? No, Nikhil, my dear rival, it is you who misunderstand the power of unity and zeal. True progress requires sacrifice, but I assure you, it is a sacrifice for a greater good.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your assurances mean little to me, Sandip. The people of these lands do not need a savior—they need a leader who respects their rights and dignity. Your zeal is nothing more than a facade for your true motives.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Rival, your concerns are misplaced. The people yearn for a leader who can ignite their spirit and lead them to greatness. Your tenants will understand the brilliance of my vision once they see the fruits of our labor.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your vision may inspire some, Sandip, but it also blinds you to the reality of suffering and exploitation. I will not stand idly by while you undermine the stability and rights of my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, your heart is as heavy as your rhetoric is dull. The people will see through your apathy and embrace the fire that I bring. Let us not forget who will be remembered as the true visionary.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words ring hollow, Sandip. The people may be swayed by your rhetoric, but I will not abandon my duty to protect them from your schemes.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your duty, my dear friend, is a burden of your own making. The people will soon see that your tenants are better off under my guidance, even if they cannot see it now.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not allow my tenants to suffer under your guise of progress. Your actions have consequences, and you will face the repercussions of your tyranny.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your tenants are like children who cannot see the candy for the sugar coating. They will thank me for the sweetness of progress, even if you cannot taste the irony.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
